newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki retreats as UK rate hike tames bulls.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki retreats as UK rate hike tames bulls.

text.p: Shares fell on Wednesday as a key rate rise in Britain boosted general unease, with coming U.S. data and elections undermining sentiment and broad equity markets already looking toppy after recent gains, brokers said.
The HEX index ended down 0.35 percent at 2,191.6 with volume a slack 335 million markka, 35 percent of it in Nokia.
Most brokers saw underlying demand for shares but said trade would remain sluggish near-term: "I think this gloom will continue at least until the elections," said one.
U.S. October unemployment due on Friday is another focus.
"There is a lot of money -- like among insurers -- waiting for the right buying opportunity," said another broker. But there are wide fears an end to recent rallies could be near.
Forest industry shares drifted lower amid sustained worries about the sector's outlook next year.
Kemira fell in relatively lively profit-taking, but held above its 49.50 markka issue price last week, touching a 49.60 session low and closing at 49.90, down 0.10.
Nokia closed almost unchanged at 207.60 markka, up 0.10.
But bank group Merita picked up after recently correcting down, adding 0.40 markka to 13.40.
